speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings following your tympanoplasty. Can you tell me more about the nature of this pain and when it started relative to your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any clicking or popping sounds in your right ear when you open your mouth or swallow? I also need to know if the pain radiates to your jaw or if you have noticed any tenderness in front of your ear.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain feel like it originates deep in the ear canal or does it radiate from the jaw joint area? I would also like to examine the surgical site for any signs of infection or granulation tissue. REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal otoscopy and pain triggered by eating, I suspect temporomandibular joint dysfunction rather than an ear complication. Do you experience any clicking, popping, or locking sensations in your jaw when you open or close your mouth?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any tenderness when I press on the muscles of mastication or the temporomandibular joint itself? I also need to know if you grind your teeth at night or clench your jaw during the day due to stress.

speaker: Patient
text: {'General': 'Denies fever or weight loss.', 'ENT': 'Reports shooting pain and discomfort in the right ear. Denies neck pain or facial tenderness.', 'Neurological': 'Denies dizziness, loss of consciousness.'}

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you deny jaw tenderness and TMJ symptoms, the shooting pain with eating strongly suggests auriculotemporal neuralgia, likely due to nerve irritation during your tympanoplasty. I will proceed with a diagnosis based on this clinical presentation. DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia
